You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The `RandomStringUtils.random(int, int, int, boolean, boolean, char[], Random)` method in the `org.apache.commons.lang3.RandomStringUtils` class is responsible for generating random strings based on the provided parameters. It creates a random character array using the given range of characters and random source.

In the failing test `RandomStringUtilsTest.testExceptions()`, the test cases aim to test exception handling when invalid parameters are passed to the `random` method. Specifically, the test checks for exceptions when negative lengths or empty arrays are provided.

The current bug report describes an issue in line 250 of the `random` method where an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` occurs when `end` is 0 or the character array is empty. This is due to the calculation `ch = chars[random.nextInt(gap) + start];` which tries to access an index within an empty array or outside the bounds when `end` is 0.

To address this issue, the calculation for generating the random character needs to be adjusted to handle cases where the array is empty or when `end` is 0. It may involve adding checks to ensure the array is non-empty and `end` is non-zero before attempting to access an index within the array.

Based on the diagnosis, the method that needs to be fixed is:
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.RandomStringUtils.random(int, int, int, boolean, boolean, char[], java.util.Random)`
